request: Employees pick a request topic from presets the organization curates (VPN, Claude, Question, Other for staff; Access, Other for clients), and the screens say Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed

findings.claim: TC-02-E2E-01 asserts what the add/rename modal draws when renaming, but its steps never open a rename modal, and no data-testid names the Rename control the screen draws — so the assertion cannot be observed and two Required ids never get the half of their contract that says 'absent'.

witness.detail: Steps (cases.md:457-461): 'Sign in as an admin. Follow the Settings > Request topics navigation row. Switch to the client audience and back. Add a staff topic, then attempt to add a second with the same name in a different case. Archive a topic from its row, then restore it from the archived list.' — no rename step. Expected Result (cases.md:464): 'The audience control is drawn when adding and not when renaming.' The Required data-testid table obliges that observation twice: contracts.md:279 'request-topic-audience | present when adding, absent when renaming' and contracts.md:280 'request-topic-type | present when adding, absent when renaming'. The screen mock draws a [ Rename ] control on every row (contracts.md:314-318), and the testid table (contracts.md:266-296) names ids for add, archive, restore, up and down but none for rename; CLAUDE.md, 'Testing': 'Selectors are data-testid only, and the ids are named in the specs.' TC-02-E2E-01 is the only case that names request-topic-audience or request-topic-type, so no other case reaches the state either.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a rename step to TC-02-E2E-01 that opens the rename modal from a row, and add the row's rename control to the Required data-testid table with the id the case selects on; or drop the rename sentence from the Expected Result and reduce the 'absent when renaming' half of contracts.md:279-280 to what a case can see.

findings.symbol: 02-request-topics.contracts.md — Screens, the ordering controls (with REQ-02-009 and Known Gaps row 5)
findings.claim: What sortOrder the up and down controls send is not stated, and the two readings the text allows differ materially: one moves the row, the other is a visible no-op.

witness.detail: contracts.md:325-329: 'Ordering is the up and down controls the DS gaps table commits to... Each control issues one PATCH .../request-topics/{topicId} carrying that row's new sortOrder.' The spec never says how that value is computed, and 02-request-topics.md:308 forecloses the obvious escape: 'a move is one PATCH of one row's sortOrder, and two rows sharing a value fall to the name tiebreak' — so a two-row swap is out. REQ-02-009 (02-request-topics.md:124): 'ordered by sortOrder ascending and, for equal values, by name ascending case-insensitively.' Seeded staff rows are VPN(10), Claude(20), Repository(30) (contracts.md:226-228). Press up on Repository. Reading A — send the neighbour's value, 20: the catalogue returns VPN, Claude, Repository, because the 20-tie breaks on name and 'Claude' < 'Repository'. The row did not move and the user sees nothing happen. Reading B — send a value strictly between, e.g. 19: the catalogue returns VPN, Repository, Claude. Both satisfy 'that row's new sortOrder'. No case decides it: TC-02-E2E-01 (cases.md:466-467) asserts only that the up and down controls are drawn or absent and never presses one, and TC-02-INT-22 (cases.md:445-447) PATCHes a caller-computed value directly rather than exercising the control.

findings.suggestedFix: State the value the control sends — e.g. the moved row takes the neighbour's sortOrder minus (or plus) one, and the audience's rows are renumbered by tens on seed and on create so a gap always exists — and add an observation that pressing up actually reorders the list.

findings.claim: This spec replaces the status vocabulary of GET .../requests and says an unknown status value is rejected, but declares no status the route answers when it is — the Routes row for that route carries 200, 403 and 404 and no 400.

witness.detail: contracts.md:21 declares the whole answer set for the amended route: '| GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests | session, org scope | 200 | 403 REQUEST_MESSAGES.scopeForbidden; 404 |'. contracts.md:110 amends its vocabulary: 'status gains the value closed (REQ-02-027) alongside the five it already accepts and all.' cases.md:146 makes rejection this spec's own rule: 'nonsense is rejected rather than defaulted.' The route rejects with 400 today — `sed -n '169,180p' apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts` prints: "const queryFields: Record<string, string> = {}; if (scope === null) queryFields.scope = 'unknown_value'; if (status === null) queryFields.status = 'unknown_value'; if (type === null) queryFields.type = 'unknown_value'; if (scope === null || status === null || type === null) { throw new BadRequestException({ error: 'validation_error', fields: queryFields }); }" — so a reachable state (?status=nonsense) has an answer in the code, a rule in the cases, and no status in the contract. The same row omits the 400 the route already answers for an unknown scope and an unknown type, and contracts.md:20 lists four 400 messages for POST .../requests while that route also emits REQUEST_MESSAGES.titleRequired, titleTooShort, titleTooLong, descriptionTooLong, priorityUnknown, neededByInvalid, neededByPast, assigneeInvalid, assigneeInactive and projectUnavailable (packages/validation/src/index.ts:1842-1854), every one of them against a field this spec's own request body still carries (contracts.md:72-82).

findings.suggestedFix: Give the GET .../requests row the 400 it answers, and say in the Errors column what an unknown status, scope or type returns and in what shape; and state on the POST .../requests row that every 400 it emits today for title, description, priority, neededBy, assignee and project is unchanged, naming those exports, so a reader of this document alone knows the amended contract in full.

findings.symbol: 02-request-topics.contracts.md — Screens mock and Required data-testid table
findings.claim: The Settings mock draws a [ Rename ] control on every row and the Required data-testid table names no id for it, so the one control that opens the create/rename modal for an existing topic has no selector.

witness.detail: contracts.md:314-318 draw '[ Rename ] [ Archive ]' on every active row and '[ Restore ]' on the archived one. The testid table (contracts.md:266-296) carries request-topics-add-btn, request-topic-row-{id}-up-btn, -down-btn, -archive-btn and -restore-btn, and no rename id. This is the same defect R1 files as an unobservable expected result; it is recorded separately because the repair is a table row rather than a case step.

findings.suggestedFix: Add request-topic-row-{id}-rename-btn to the Required data-testid table with its presence rule.

findings.claim: The empty-picker copy tells the user two things this spec's own rules make false: that there are no topics yet, and that an admin is who adds one.

witness.detail: contracts.md:130 fixes the text: 'There are no request topics yet. An admin can add one in Settings.' REQ-02-017 (02-request-topics.md:168) fires it 'WHILE the audience of the form's addressee has no ACTIVE topic', and edge case 13 (contracts.md:405) reaches exactly that with topics present: 'The catalogue's last active staff topic is archived | ... the new-request picker shows REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.pickerEmpty' — 'yet' is false there, and TC-02-E2E-06 (cases.md:533-534) is the case that produces the screen. Separately the permission matrix (02-request-topics.md:57) grants manage-request-topics to admin and manager, so 'An admin can add one' understates who the reader may ask. Filed as a note: the copy misleads, but no implementation is ambiguous.

findings.suggestedFix: Reword to something true in both states and for both grantees, e.g. 'No request topics are available. An admin or manager can add one in Settings.'

findings.claim: The sortOrder clamp is the one validation rule with no case, and it is also the only rule in the table whose refusal is silent.

witness.detail: contracts.md:251: '| 6 | topic sortOrder | Optional integer, 0-32767 | REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.nameRequired is not used here; an out-of-range value is clamped to the bound | yes |'. Rules 1-5 and 7-10 each have a case (TC-02-UNIT-01/02/03, TC-02-INT-04/05/06/12/13/18 and TC-02-INT-11); no case sends a sortOrder outside 0-32767, so a build that rejected it with 400, or stored it unclamped, would pass every case here. The Data Model gives the column no CHECK either (contracts.md:175).

findings.suggestedFix: Add the out-of-range sortOrder to TC-02-INT-03's steps and its expected clamped value, or say in the row that the clamp is deliberately unobserved and why.

findings.claim: REQ-02-026 adds a topicId query parameter to GET .../requests, a shipping route, and the Summary names the classifier change and the status vocabulary but not the new filter.

witness.detail: REQ-02-026 (02-request-topics.md:241) and contracts.md:110 ('Query gains topicId') change the contract of a route that already ships. The Summary (02-request-topics.md:26-39) names the catalogue, the audience, the snapshot, the retirement of accessKind on the way in, and the four status words; it does not name a topic filter on the list. The request named presets and the four words and did not ask for filtering. A note rather than a blocker: an optional query parameter costs no existing caller, and the Requests list mock (contracts.md:352) already draws the control.

findings.suggestedFix: One clause in the Summary saying the list gains a topic filter, so a person confirms it was wanted.

findings.claim: The schema an implementer reads while building this says spec 02 is where a request gains a client addressee, and this spec says spec 03 is.

witness.detail: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1143 carries the comment "/// 'member' is the only valid value in this spec; spec 02 adds `client`." on Request.assigneeKind. REQ-02-020's decision table (02-request-topics.md:198) declares 'domains=(topicAudience: staff|client, assigneeKind: member)' and 02-request-topics.md:203 says 'member is the only addressee kind a request may carry as this spec ships', with Known Gaps (02-request-topics.md:304) placing the client addressee in spec 03. The behaviour this spec specifies is the safe one; the note exists because whoever implements it will read that comment beside the column and may wire the second kind in.

findings.suggestedFix: Nothing in this spec. Worth a person knowing that the schema comment predicts the wrong spec number, so the implementer of 02 is not surprised by it.
